mark: Its indexer top-k bench on the image: gain beyond the interval, bit-exact; long prefill not worse
evidence: README section 3 on the candidate image, two boots: pytest --noconftest -q on test_deepseek_v41_tilelang.py, test_deepseek_v4_1_lsa.py, test_deepseek_v4_1_attention.py, then deepseek_v41_indexer_reads.py; and bench_2boot.py (verify_exactness, then the paired base/cand latency grid). The bench's baseline module is 1107's indexer.py mounted at /tmp_host/indexer_baseline.py. Verbatim, it cannot import on the candidate image (the image's gemm.py no longer exports _e2m1_code after #991), so the scored runs use 1107's indexer.py with 1107 gemm.py's _e2m1_code inlined (indexer_baseline_1107.diff). That function feeds only 1107's quantizer kernels, which the bench does not call; the IndexerTopK code under test is 1107's, unchanged. The same command on the 1107 image was also run, twice

pytest_candidate-49.boot1: 139 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed in 328.89s; indexer reads: scored 4 cases
pytest_candidate-49.boot2: 139 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed in 330.51s; indexer reads: scored 4 cases

measured.selection_cells: 210 (base,cand) pairs over N=64K..1M x M=1..1024 plus the 16K reindex row; 209 are faster beyond the two-boot interval, 1 is slower beyond it
measured.worse_cell: standalone IndexerTopK(1048576, 512, 1) at N=524288, M=1: 38.92/39.17 -> 40.51/40.59 us (0.963x). The PR's tables do not report this selector; at N=1M M=1 and every M>=6 it is faster
measured.same_command_on_1107: exit 1 on both boots inside verify_exactness: 1107's IndexerTopK has no gather_scores path, so cand_plan.select.run(..., gather=...) fails with 'indexer_topk_segment.Active is expected to have non-NULL pointer'. No A/A floor comes from it
measured.readme_command_verbatim: exit 1: ImportError cannot import name '_e2m1_code' from the candidate image's tilelang/gemm.py
measured.interval: two candidate-image boots per arm, each arm a trimmed mean of 25 timed calls; a gain is beyond the interval when the slower candidate boot is faster than the faster baseline boot

parts.part: indexer top-k bench: gain beyond the interval
parts.detail: 209 of 210 cells faster beyond the two-boot interval, magnitudes within a few percent of the PR's sp7 tables; one standalone selector cell not on the Layer 20 path is 4% slower at N=512K M=1
verify_exactness PASS on both boots (indices, values and counts torch.equal against 1107's IndexerTopK, plus Layer 20 gather_scores against the full-width select)
a suite metric of the tp3-switched cluster run, not of a single-GPU bench

verdict_scope: sp8-evaluable parts only; long prefill is cannot-evaluate-on-sp8
reason: On the integrated image the PR's own bench reproduces its top-k gains against 1107's selector, beyond the two-boot interval in 209 of 210 cells, with exact outputs, and its test suite passes on both boots. Running it needed a one-line import shim because #991 removed the 1107 helper the baseline file imports.
notes: commands.txt start_utc is when the command was issued and includes any wait on /tmp/spark-lab-gpu.lock
The pytest count differs from the PR's 132 because the candidate's test files also carry #993's and #991's tests
bench-analysis.json is derived from the two candidate bench JSONs (json/) by a999.py

The 1 skipped test in test_deepseek_v41_tilelang.py is, by #993's -v run of the same file on the same image, test_indexer_reads_only_visible_rows (no compute-sanitizer in the image); with the host sanitizer mounted it passes on this image (pr-993/sanitizer-candidate49-boot*.txt)
